newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end up on telcom sector, Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end up on telcom sector, Greenspan.

text.p: Brazilian shares ended up 0.89 percent, buoyed by the telecommunications sector and comments by U.S. Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan which boosted Wall Street stock prices, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active stocks closed at 79,049 points. Market turnover was a moderate 449.8 million reais ($432.5 million).
Benchmark Telebras preferred rose 1.23 percent to 90.70 reais, while Telesp preferred gained 1.63 percent to 249.50 reais.

Earlier today Morgan Stanley released a report saying it had raised its year-end target price for Telebras and its main subsidiaries. Its 1997 target price for Telebras was raised to $115 from $85.88, while Telesp was raised to $300 from $237.

Analysts also saw as positive news that the Brazilian government is now aiming to hold on January 28 a first lower house vote on a bill allowing President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for a second term.
"If the government succeeds in having the first full vote next week, it may signal that an agreement has been reached with the PMDB party," one said.
The federal government has been trying to convince members of the PMDB, Congress' largest party, to vote on the re-election before February 15 as the party's convention recommended.
State mining giant Vale do Rio Doce ended up 0.04 percent at 24.65 reais. Oil state firm Petrobras dropped 0.77 percent to 193.50 reais.
Power firm Eletrobras preferred shares rose 1.86 percent to close at 437 reais.
Caemi preferred shares fell 4.1 percent to end at 46.99 percent after the company denied press reports that it was being sold to two foreign mining firms.
The bolsa's Eletrical Energy Index of the nine most liquid power shares rose 1.15 percent to close at 2,285 points.
The market's wider Brazil index (IBX) of 100 leading shares ended at 1,714 points, up 1.05 percent.
